extracted.intended_audience: Researchers (Spokesperson PIs and collaborating PIs) preparing LOIs and full proposals for the Simons Collaborations in Ecology & Evolution funding opportunity
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and requirements for submitting a Vision Statement (LOI) and full proposal to the Simons Collaborations in Ecology & Evolution program, including eligibility, required proposal components, formatting, budget guidance, data-sharing expectations, and application workflows in SAM. Targets formation of multi-PI, cross-disciplinary collaborative grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vision statement content (big idea and hypotheses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Vision statements should clearly outline the big idea and hypotheses that the proposed collaboration will address, including high-level overviews of the methods and approaches that will be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vision statements should address which disciplines and subdisciplines will be brought together, how research efforts extrapolate across scales, why the work is uniquely suited for Simons funding, why initiation is timely, and why it would be difficult to obtain funding for this question elsewhere. Propose investigators who may be included and an estimated anticipated overall yearly total cost. Use the provided SAM template; narrative must not exceed two pages single-spaced size 11 text with 0.5-inch margins; one additional page may be used for figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: fundamental, idea-generating research (not applied-only)
rubrics_metrics.description: This call is interested in bold and cutting-edge, idea-generating research that focuses on a fundamental understanding of genetic, ecological and evolutionary factors shaping dynamics of organisms and/or communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied research that does not seek fundamental insights is not appropriate. Disease-related projects are within scope only if they aim to understand basic eco-evolutionary principles; projects aiming to develop treatment strategies are out of scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-disciplinary integration and scale
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority will be given to cross-disciplinary collaborations that integrate levels of scale (e.g., genes to species to communities, local to global processes, ecological and evolutionary timescales).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects that cut across fields/subfields, diverse methodological approaches, or geographic regions are of interest. Collaborations should bring unique combinations of expertise to generate fundamental understanding; outstanding proposals will catalyze impactful conversations across disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open sharing of data, code, analysis pipelines, protocols and reagents
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators in a Simons Collaboration are expected to openly share data, code, analysis pipelines, protocols and reagents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full proposals must include a 1-page Data storage, computation and sharing plan describing types/amounts of data, where they will be stored (short- and long-term), who will have access, timeline for access, how access will be managed, when/how analysis pipelines will be shared, and computational facility needs. Reference the foundation’s Policy on Data and Renewable Reagent Sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator eligibility (degrees, position, research space)
rubrics_metrics.description: All investigators must hold a Ph.D. or equivalent degree and have a faculty position or the equivalent (eligible for receiving grant funding as a PI) at a college, university, research institute or other research facility. In addition, eligible applicants must have research space at their institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications may be submitted by domestic and foreign nonprofit organizations, public and private institutions, state/local government units, and research-oriented federal agencies. There are no citizenship requirements for PIs. Simons Foundation W-2 employees (including Flatiron Institute employees) may not apply as PIs or be listed among personnel who will receive funded compensation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions for China / Hong Kong institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: SF and SFI do not provide funding to institutions in China (including institutions in Hong Kong), or to fiscal sponsors or agents of institutions in China or Hong Kong. This includes funding to support subcontracts at institutions in China or Hong Kong or consultants residing or working for institutions in China or Hong Kong.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team composition and seniority diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are expected to include investigators at multiple levels of seniority and across academic disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number of PIs should be driven by needed expertise; smaller or larger collaborations will be considered. PIs may be grouped into subteams to facilitate communication and sharing. The LOI should include a list of PIs with summaries of expertise (beginning with the Spokesperson PI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-institutional expectation (not single-institution)
rubrics_metrics.description: This call is not intended for single-institution support; scope is expected to involve PIs from multiple institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assemble the strongest scientific team regardless of geographic location or institutional affiliation. Collaboration PIs may be added/changed between LOI and full proposal stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal novelty, timeliness, and transformative potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Vision statements should explain why and how the support of a collaborative research project from the Simons Foundation will transform understanding of ecological and evolutionary dynamics; why the work is timely; and why it is uniquely suited for Simons support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why it would be difficult to obtain funding to investigate this question from other agencies/foundations; emphasize novelty and opportunity for breakthroughs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget guidance and expectations (LOI estimate and full budgets)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an estimated anticipated overall yearly total cost in the LOI. Funding levels per collaboration are guideline $1–4 million USD per year, inclusive of twenty percent indirect costs; total program budget $8M/year to support up to 1–3 collaborations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A full detailed budget is required at the full proposal stage. On the Spokesperson PI application include a 1-page Budget narrative providing broad overview of allocations and how funding will be distributed among PIs/shared resources. Use SAM budget tab to add detailed budget and provide justification in the budget's justification text boxes (no separate upload).

rubrics_metrics.name: Full proposal required components and page limits / formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Full proposals must include specific sections and use specified formatting: a 12-page Scientific narrative (including figures; references below), 1-page Collaboration and leadership plan, 1-page Data storage/computation/sharing plan, Individual Contributions (≤250 words per PI), 1-page Budget narrative, and biosketches for each PI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use single-spaced, size 11 Times New Roman text, 0.5-inch margins. Label each section clearly and maintain the section order specified. Biosketches must be SciENcv or fillable PDF NIH-/NSF-style. File naming conventions: 'Last Name_First Name_Biosketch' and 'Last Name_First Name_Other Support' for other support files.

rubrics_metrics.name: LOI formatting and template use
rubrics_metrics.description: Vision Statements will be submitted as Letters of Intent (LOIs) in SAM and must use the provided template available in SAM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific vision statement narrative must not exceed two pages single-spaced size 11 text with 0.5-inch margins. One additional page allowed for figures. The SAM template includes specific instructions for multiple sections with individual length limits; follow them closely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listing of PIs and number-of-PIs consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: LOI must include a List of PIs with Summaries of Expertise, beginning with the Spokesperson PI. Enter the Number of PIs included in this LOI (including the Spokesperson).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The number entered must match the number of PIs for whom summaries are included. All PIs other than the Spokesperson must be listed in the Project Personnel section of the Contacts & Personnel tab. This number is not binding and may change at the full proposal stage if invited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosketch and other support requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Spokesperson PI must upload a SciENcv or fillable PDF NIH- or NSF-style biosketch at the LOI stage; biosketches for all PIs are required at the full proposal stage. For each PI upload Other Support using NSF, NIH or SciENcv template and indicate overlap (or write 'no overlap').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All biosketch and other support files will be uploaded under the Spokesperson PI's application. Use specified file naming conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project personnel roles and SAM listing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Project personnel include individuals who contribute substantively to the scientific development or execution of a project. The Simons Foundation does not use the role type co-PI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project personnel on the Spokesperson PI application should reflect only those specific to the Spokesperson PI’s project, not those of other PIs. Project personnel for each Collaboration PI must be listed under that PI’s sub-application; subcontract personnel under subcontract sections. See SAM FAQs for multi-site/collaboration and subcontract setup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional sign-off and submission workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutional signing official and financial officer are required at the full application stage. Each PI must Send for sign-off to their institution's signing official; signing official signs and submits. For the Spokesperson PI, after all PI sub-applications are Submitted to Spokesperson PI and Signed — Pending Submission, the Spokesperson PI must click Submit Application Package to submit to the foundation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Spokesperson PI's institutional official cannot submit the package to the foundation; only the Spokesperson PI can submit. Subcontracts do not require a subcontract institution's signature within SAM. Use Check Application Progress to view missing required information before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data storage, computation and sharing plan (full proposal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a 1-page Data storage, computation and sharing plan describing types/amounts of data and/or renewable reagents, where they will be stored short- and long-term, who will have access and the timeline for providing access, how access will be managed, how/when analysis pipelines will be shared, computational facility needs, and who will take responsibility for data management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please reference the foundation’s Policy on Data and Renewable Reagent Sharing. This plan is mandatory at full proposal stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership and collaboration plan (1 page)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a 1-page Collaboration and leadership plan describing the leadership plan and PI roles/responsibilities, how decisions about scientific priorities will be made and by whom, the communication structure, and any project management tools to be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the collaboration will ensure optimal communication among members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual contributions (per-PI description)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a description of each PI's role in the collaboration and how the goals align with their current/planned research; include each PI's relevant expertise. Limit descriptions to 250 or fewer words per PI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include these in the full proposal as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and file naming conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific formatting (font, spacing, margins) and naming conventions are required for uploaded files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use single-spaced, size 11 Times New Roman text with 0.5-inch margins. Use naming conventions such as 'Last Name_First Name_Biosketch' and 'Last Name_First Name_Other Support'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generative AI disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate the extent to which, if any, generative AI technology was used and how it was used to develop your proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This disclosure is requested both for LOI and full proposal uploads where indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process and review stages
rubrics_metrics.description: Vision statements will be reviewed by the Simons Foundation with input from outside reviewers. 10–20 spokesperson PIs will be invited to submit full proposals. Full proposals will be reviewed with input from outside reviewers; finalists will be invited to present to the review committee before award selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared for external peer review and a potential presentation to a review committee if selected as finalist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable systems and theoretical/computational work
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no restrictions on biological systems used; proposals may include plants, microbes, invertebrates, vertebrates, and purely theoretical or computational research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus must remain on fundamental eco-evolutionary principles rather than solely applied aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: PI effort expectations and multiple-submission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: While no minimum percent effort is required, Simons expects PIs to commit substantial time reflecting a leading role and significant engagement. An individual may be listed as a non-spokesperson PI on multiple submissions but may be the spokesperson PI on only one submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other support disclosure and overlap indication
rubrics_metrics.description: For each PI, upload a list of other support using NSF, NIH or SciENcv template and include an indication of overlap for each award (or write 'no overlap').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All other support files are uploaded under the Spokesperson PI's application; use the naming convention 'Last Name_First Name_Other Support'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational assurances (IRB/IACUC)
rubrics_metrics.description: On each application, indicate if the application requires organizational assurances (IRB and/or IACUC).

rubrics_metrics.name: SAM account and submission mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: All applicants must use the Simons Award Manager (SAM) to submit applications. Vision statements and full proposals are created and submitted via SAM under the Spokesperson PI's account; the Submit Application button finalizes submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If new to SAM, register before creating an application. If you have a ProposalCentral account, a SAM profile may already exist—use 'Forgot Password?' to set a new password. Instructional videos on using SAM are available. Check Application Progress to find missing required information; you cannot submit after the deadline. For assistance contact the provided technical assistance email.
